Evidence: MIT license, 194 files, 22 purpose-specific keyword hits, and 8/8 bounded checks passed; no dependency installation or production access occurred. Risks: parser fidelity, transitive dependencies, maintenance cadence, and provenance/security review remain unresolved. Smallest reversible prototype is one disposable-workspace conversion with diff and provenance checklist. Metric: editor review time and accepted-content throughput. Time-to-learn: one working session. No adoption or implementation is recommended.

Retain two fleet product opportunities as deferred specifications only: execution-integrity control plane and AI cost-to-learn gate. Existing records show 108 approved proposals without execution, 63% approved-proposal execution rate, 21 failed requests, 7 open repairs, and September AI usage of $950.44418695 across 5,316 calls. These support workflow-risk hypotheses, not ROI or causal claims. Do not admit implementation until capacity clears and CTO/CFO review the reversible prototypes.
